description: An end-of-game unit: fires when the board is almost full. Strongest with one empty cell left (41 stones), and with 40 stones. Earlier it fires mainly when the player to move went first (even stone count) and only one or two columns are still open. With an odd stone count before 40 it is suppressed, even if the board is nearly full. It does not care which side is winning or about threats.
effect: None measurable. Forcing it to max or zero moves column probabilities by at most about 0.06 in endgames and about 0.10 in one early position.
notes: Best dev F1 0.665 for 'only one legal column' (p1). The submitted program p6 (ply>=40, or first player with one open column, or first player at ply>=38 with <=2 open) scored F1 0.663 (P 0.81, R 0.56, AUROC 0.78), simulation share 0.07. Minimal pairs: from a ply-34 position, every ply-36 continuation fired (1.9-6.5) and every ply-35/37 one did not, so parity matters. Columns filled artificially by ply 24 did not fire. Rules that used only the stone count or the open-column count stayed at F1 0.55-0.63. There is a small group of early-game firings (ply 5-13) that is not explained. The leftover variance between games is unexplained and the exact column identity may matter.
